description: NYC facade typologies for the NYCSim facade classifier (pipeline) and facade kit (Blender). `facade_class` is the int16 written to buildings.parquet (DATA_CONTRACTS §5). `materials` = [primary, secondary] using the §5 material_primary names; `window_type` names the kit window piece family (blender/common/facade_params.py WINDOW_TYPES); `floors_typical` = [min,max]; `era` = [year_from, year_to]; `features` name the kit piece families the placer should attach; `boroughs_typical` MN/BX/BK/QN/SI; `pluto_classes_typical` = MapPLUTO bldgclass prefixes most often mapped here. Heights are real published NYC norms: Old-Law tenement floor 3.0 m, New-Law 3.1 m, brownstone parlour 3.7 m / upper 3.0 m, prewar apartment 2.9 m, post-war 2.65 m, office 1970 3.7 m, office 2010 4.2 m, curtain-wall module 3.9 m, supertall residential 3.3–3.6 m.

classes.name: Old Law tenement (dumbbell), red brick, 5 floors, fire escape
classes.description: 25 × 100 ft lot dumbbell tenement: 4 windows across, segmental-arched brick heads with brownstone sills, pressed-metal bracketed cornice, iron fire escape on the street face, ground floor storefronts with roll-down gates. Lower East Side, East Village, Harlem, Williamsburg, Bushwick, Mott Haven.

classes.name: New Law tenement, buff/red brick with limestone trim, 6 floors
classes.description: 40–50 ft wide New Law tenement with light courts, limestone base and keystoned lintels, galvanised-iron cornice with dentils; Washington Heights, Inwood, Grand Concourse side streets, Crown Heights, Astoria.

classes.name: Italianate / Neo-Grec brownstone rowhouse, 4 floors over basement, high stoop
classes.description: 20 ft wide brownstone: rusticated basement, 10–12 step stoop rising 2.4 m to a parlour floor with 2/2 or 1/1 sashes under bracketed lintels, heavy bracketed cornice, cast-iron areaway railing and newel posts. Park Slope, Bedford-Stuyvesant, Fort Greene, Harlem, Upper West Side side streets.

classes.name: Early Italianate rowhouse, brownstone or brick with brownstone trim, 3 floors, stoop
classes.description: Lower 3-storey Italianate rowhouse, 6–8 step stoop, simple bracketed cornice; Cobble Hill, Carroll Gardens, Chelsea, Clinton Hill.

classes.name: Renaissance Revival limestone rowhouse with bow front, 4 floors
classes.description: Bow-fronted limestone rowhouse with low stoop, carved string courses and swag-and-garland cornice; Crown Heights, Prospect Lefferts, Hamilton Heights, Riverside Drive side streets.

classes.name: Federal rowhouse, Flemish-bond red brick, 2.5–3 floors, dormers
classes.description: Charlton-King-Vandam, Greenwich Village, Brooklyn Heights Federal houses: Flemish bond, 6/6 sashes with stone lintels, low stoop with wrought-iron rail, pitched roof with two dormers.

classes.name: Greek Revival rowhouse, brick with brownstone basement and trim, 3 floors
classes.description: Washington Square North / Brooklyn Heights type: brownstone basement, Doric-pilastered doorway, 6/6 sashes shortened per floor, dentilled fascia cornice, anthemion ironwork.

classes.name: Prewar elevator apartment house, red/tan brick on limestone base, 6–12 floors
classes.description: Upper West Side / Grand Concourse / Jackson Heights prewar: two-storey limestone base, brick shaft with quoins, casement pairs, terracotta or stone cornice or brick parapet, canopied entrance, cedar water tower.

classes.name: Beaux-Arts apartment house, limestone and brick, 10–14 floors
classes.description: Riverside Drive / West End Avenue / Fifth Avenue Beaux-Arts: rusticated 3-storey limestone base, brick shaft with stone quoins and balconettes, deep copper cornice, sometimes mansard with dormers.

classes.name: Art Deco apartment house, tan/brown brick, corner casements, 6 floors
classes.description: Grand Concourse / Pelham Parkway / Ocean Parkway Deco: polychrome brick banding, wrap-around corner casements, stepped parapet, mosaic-and-stainless entry with canopy.

classes.name: Post-war white glazed brick apartment tower, 15–25 floors
classes.description: Upper East Side / Murray Hill / Kips Bay white-brick: glazed white brick, aluminium sliders with through-wall AC sleeves, cantilevered concrete balconies, plain parapet, enclosed water tank on the roof.

classes.name: Post-war red brick elevator apartment, 6 floors
classes.description: Forest Hills / Rego Park / Riverdale / Flatbush 6-storey brick elevator building with casements replaced by aluminium sliders, cast-stone coping, brick parapet.

classes.name: NYCHA public-housing tower, red/brown brick, 13–21 floors
classes.description: Tower-in-the-park cross / Y / slab plan, unadorned red brick, regular punched aluminium sliders, concrete slab edges, elevator bulkhead.

classes.name: Mitchell-Lama / co-op slab tower, exposed concrete and brown brick, 20–35 floors
classes.description: Co-op City, Starrett City, Waterside, Big Six Towers: concrete slab edges and columns expressed, brick infill, stacked balconies.

classes.name: 1980s brown brick condominium with balconies, 20–35 floors
classes.description: Upper East Side / Midtown East 1980s condo: dark brown brick, bronze-anodised windows, projecting balconies, granite base with retail.

classes.name: Dark glass curtain-wall office tower, 1965–1985, 30–50 floors
classes.description: Sixth Avenue / Park Avenue / Water Street slab: bronze or black anodised mullions, tinted glass, spandrel glass, plaza with recessed lobby.

classes.name: Unitised clear-glass curtain-wall office tower, 2005–2025, 40–70 floors
classes.description: Hudson Yards, World Trade Center, One Vanderbilt, Downtown Brooklyn: floor-to-ceiling low-e glass, silver mullions, tall lobby, mechanical crown.

classes.name: Residential supertall, glass with metal or stone piers, 60–95 floors
classes.description: Billionaires' Row / Downtown: slender floor plate, floor-to-ceiling glass, expressed piers, crown with mechanical screens.

classes.name: International Style office, glass and metal spandrel panels, 1950–1965, 20–40 floors
classes.description: Park Avenue / Third Avenue 1950s–60s: green or grey glass, stainless or aluminium mullions, opaque spandrel panels, colonnaded ground floor.

classes.name: Cast-iron store-and-loft, 5–6 floors, tall arched windows
classes.description: SoHo / Tribeca cast-iron facade: Corinthian colonnettes each bay, tall 2/2 sashes, full-height ground floor storefront with cast-iron piers and vault lights, pedimented cornice.

classes.name: Brick industrial loft, steel sash, 6–12 floors, water tower
classes.description: Garment District / Long Island City / Dumbo / Sunset Park loft: brick piers, steel-sash 4×5 industrial windows with hopper, corbelled brick cornice, cedar water tower on steel dunnage, painted signs.

classes.name: Concrete / block warehouse, 1–3 floors, steel windows, loading docks
classes.description: Hunts Point / Maspeth / Red Hook / Port Morris: painted concrete block or precast panel, ribbon of steel sash, truck docks with bumpers and roll-up doors.

classes.name: Terracotta-clad early skyscraper, 12–20 floors, cornice
classes.description: Flatiron / Broadway–Chambers / Woolworth-era: glazed terracotta ornament, tripartite base–shaft–capital, deep projecting cornice with modillions.

classes.name: Neoclassical limestone bank, 2–4 floors, columns, tall arched windows
classes.description: Corner bank temple: granite base, engaged Ionic columns, tall arched or rectangular windows with bronze grilles, dentilled entablature.

classes.name: Art Deco setback tower, limestone/brick piers, 30–70 floors
classes.description: Chrysler / Empire State / 500 Fifth type: vertical limestone piers with recessed brick spandrels, 1916-zoning setbacks, decorative crown.

classes.name: 1916-zoning masonry office, brick and limestone, 15–35 floors
classes.description: Garment Center / Financial District / Downtown Brooklyn 1920s office: limestone base, tan brick shaft, stepped setbacks with terracotta copings.

classes.name: Two-family detached / semi-detached, vinyl or aluminium siding, 2 floors
classes.description: Middle Village / Whitestone / Canarsie / Throggs Neck: brick first floor with vinyl-sided upper floor, picture window, aluminium awnings, attached garage under, chain-link front fence.

classes.name: Brick two-family semi-detached, 2 floors, bay or paired windows
classes.description: Jackson Heights / Woodside / Pelham Bay / Bensonhurst brick two-family: soldier-course lintels, cast-stone sills, projecting bay, parapet with cast-stone coping.

classes.name: Tudor Revival attached house, brick and stucco with half-timbering, 2 floors
classes.description: Forest Hills Gardens / Jackson Heights / Fieldston / Midwood: brick base, stucco and half-timber gables, slate roof, casement windows.

classes.name: Single-family detached, aluminium/vinyl siding, 2 floors, garage
classes.description: Staten Island South Shore / Eastern Queens post-war detached: hi-ranch or colonial, siding over brick base, double garage, picture window.

classes.name: Wood-frame rowhouse re-clad in siding, 2–3 floors, cornice
classes.description: Sunset Park / Windsor Terrace / Ridgewood frame houses: original clapboard now vinyl or aluminium siding, surviving pressed-metal cornice, low stoop.

classes.name: Frame three-family with fire escape, siding or asphalt shingle, 3 floors
classes.description: Bushwick / Ridgewood / Cypress Hills frame three-family: siding, iron fire escape, corner bodega at grade.

classes.name: 2000s infill multi-family with through-wall AC sleeves ('Fedders special'), 3–4 floors
classes.description: Bushwick / Flushing / Bensonhurst 2000s speculative infill: light brick or stucco, aluminium windows with a Fedders sleeve under each, curb-cut garage, balconies with aluminium rail.

classes.name: Brick attached rowhouse, 2 floors, flat roof, bay
classes.description: Bay Ridge / Dyker Heights / Ridgewood / Wakefield 1920s brick rowhouse: tan or red brick, low stoop, one-storey bay, cast-stone coping.

classes.name: Gothic Revival church, rubble or ashlar stone, pointed-arch windows
classes.description: Manhattan schist or brownstone Gothic church: pointed traceried windows, buttresses, corner tower or spire, slate roof.

classes.name: Romanesque Revival brick church, round arches
classes.description: Brick Romanesque parish church or synagogue: round-arched windows and portals, corbelled brick cornices, campanile.

classes.name: One/two-storey commercial 'taxpayer' strip, brick, storefronts, roll gates
classes.description: Avenue taxpayer: continuous storefront bays with sign bands and roll-down gates, brick parapet, RTUs and billboard on the roof.

classes.name: Open-deck concrete parking garage, 3–8 levels
classes.description: Precast or cast-in-place garage: continuous open ribbon openings with cable rails, sloped ramps, illuminated 'PARK' sign.

classes.name: Public school (C.B.J. Snyder era), brick with limestone trim, 4–5 floors, tall windows
classes.description: H-plan or U-plan Collegiate Gothic / Renaissance school: tall triple windows per classroom, limestone banding, terracotta cornice, chain-link rooftop yard.

classes.name: Post-war public school, brick with ribbon windows, 3–4 floors
classes.description: 1950s–60s Board of Education school: buff brick, continuous aluminium ribbon windows with glazed brick spandrels, flat roof.

classes.name: Hospital / medical pavilion, glass and metal panel, 8–20 floors
classes.description: NYU Langone / Mount Sinai / Montefiore pavilions: metal panel and glass, ambulance canopy, heavy rooftop mechanical.

classes.name: Glass hotel tower, 20–50 floors, 3.2 m floors
classes.description: Midtown West / Long Island City hotel: narrow glass slab, porte-cochère canopy, rooftop bar.

classes.name: Prewar masonry hotel, brick and limestone, 15–30 floors, setbacks, water tower
classes.description: Times Square / Murray Hill 1920s hotel: limestone base with marquee canopy, brick shaft with stone banding, stepped setbacks, rooftop sign.

classes.name: FDNY firehouse, brick with limestone or cast-iron trim, 3 floors, apparatus door
classes.description: Napoleon LeBrun-era firehouse: 25 ft front, single large apparatus door with red overhead panel, ornate cornice.

classes.name: Reinforced-concrete daylight factory / loft, steel sash, 6–12 floors
classes.description: Dumbo / Industry City / Starrett-Lehigh / Hunters Point: exposed concrete frame with brick spandrel infill and wall-to-wall steel sash.

classes.name: Self-storage / light-industrial box, metal panel, 4–8 floors, few windows
classes.description: Highway-side storage building: insulated metal panel in two colours, spandrel band of fake windows, big logo.

classes.name: Big-box / supermarket, precast or CMU, 1 floor, sign band
classes.description: Gateway Center / College Point / Bruckner big box: painted precast panels, EIFS sign band, glass vestibule, parking lot in front.

classes.name: Gas station kiosk with pump canopy, 1 floor
classes.description: Convenience kiosk with glass front and a flat fluorescent-lit pump canopy on steel columns.

classes.name: Modern infill, glass and metal / fibre-cement panel, 4–7 floors
classes.description: Williamsburg / Lower East Side / Astoria 2010s infill: rain-screen metal or fibre-cement panels, large aluminium windows, recessed balconies.

classes.name: New-construction mid-rise condo / rental, glass with brick or panel piers, 6–15 floors
classes.description: Williamsburg waterfront / Long Island City / Downtown Brooklyn 2010s: floor-to-ceiling glass alternating with brick or panel piers, Juliet balconies, roof deck.

classes.name: Garden apartments, red brick, 2–3 floors, casements
classes.description: Jackson Heights / Sunnyside Gardens / Parkchester walk-ups: red brick around a courtyard, casement windows, slate or flat roofs.

classes.name: Mediterranean / Spanish Revival house, stucco, tile roof, 2 floors
classes.description: Douglaston / Dyker Heights / Todt Hill / Fieldston stucco villa: arched openings, red clay tile roof, wrought-iron balconettes.

classes.name: Rubble-stone or granite mansion / institution, 2–4 floors
classes.description: Riverdale / Snug Harbor / City College campus: Manhattan schist or granite ashlar, limestone quoins, slate roof with dormers.

classes.name: 1980s brown brick / precast office or institutional mid-rise, 6–15 floors
classes.description: Downtown Brooklyn / Kew Gardens / Fordham Road 1980s: brown brick or precast panels, bronze-tinted punched windows, granite base.

classes.name: Elevated station / transit structure, painted steel and corrugated metal
classes.description: IRT/BMT elevated station house: riveted steel columns, corrugated metal and wood-panel station house with hipped roof, canopy over platform.

classes.name: Italianate store-and-loft, marble/brownstone front with cast-iron storefront, 5 floors
classes.description: Tribeca / Ladies' Mile: Tuckahoe marble or brownstone upper facade with segmental-arched 2/2 windows and bracketed cornice over a cast-iron colonnaded storefront.
